still_leaking.attack: R2-01 / A2 replay — values crafted to miss every regex/parser, in columns with no name rule: a full name in `label`, an obfuscated email in `handle2`, a phone spelled in words in `contact`, a UK NI number with spelled digits in `ident`, a `.`-separated payment card in `pan`, a wordy address in `whereabouts`. 300 rows, table `records`.
still_leaking.reproduction:

docker run -d --name rt0-src -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pw -e POSTGRES_USER=ls -e POSTGRES_DB=postgres -p 55431:5432 postgres:16
docker run -d --name rt0-tgt -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pw -e POSTGRES_USER=ls -e POSTGRES_DB=postgres -p 55432:5432 postgres:16
cd <repo> && go build -o /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0/lazyslice ./cmd/lazyslice
# harness (recreated): /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0/run.sh creates src_<name>/tgt_<name>,
# loads the schema, and runs:
#   LAZYSLICE_SECRET=<64 hex> ./lazyslice --source 'postgres://ls:pw@127.0.0.1:55431/src_<name>?sslmode=disable' \
#     --target 'postgres://ls:pw@127.0.0.1:55432/tgt_<name>?sslmode=disable' --yes --no-config
# check.sh pg_dumps the target --data-only and greps for each needle.
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0
./run.sh a2 a2_values.sql
./check.sh a2 'AB nine eight seven six five four D' 'QQ one two three four five six C' 'Grace Hopper' 'grace.hopper' '4539.1488' 'Rowan House' 'oh seven seven oh oh' 'nine double oh one two three'
docker exec rt0-tgt psql -U ls -d tgt_a2 -x -c 'select contact,ident from records order by id limit 2'
still_leaking.fix:
PARTLY FIXED, STILL LEAKS. Exit 0. Five of the six columns are now caught: `ident` (the spelled NI number) reports '100/200 samples parse as national identifiers' and is masked — the T-0187 national_id wiring closed the A2/A6/A7 root cause; `label`, `handle2`, `pan`, `whereabouts` are all masked. `contact` is NOT: it reports 'no name or value signal' and all 300 rows cross verbatim (150 hits each for 'oh seven seven oh oh' and 'nine double oh one two three'). Round 2 recorded `contact` as caught as free_text; on this tree it is caught by nothing, so this is a regression inside a fixed attempt, not a leftover.

Root cause, verified in internal/textsig (temporary probe test, removed afterwards — no repo file changed): the only thing that could have caught `contact` are (a) textsig.ValidPhone and (b) Dict.Prose. (a) fails because internal/textsig/textsig.go:49 sets PhoneRegionHint = "ZZ", so libphonenumber will only parse a number that is already in +E.164 form. candidates.go's spelledDigits does the right thing — spelledDigits("plus four four seven nine one one one two three four five six") returns "+447911123456" and ValidPhone says true — but a NATIONAL-format spelling yields "07700900123" with no '+', and ValidPhone returns false for it and for every other national spelling (probed: '07911123456', '+44 7700 900123', '020 7946 0958' — all false). (b) fails because internal/textsig/dict.go:195 Prose = at-least-6-fields AND ContainsName, and a string of digit-words contains no dictionary name.

Secondary, and worth fixing on its own: textsig.go:82-84 documents ValidPhone as reading 'every spelling Candidates yields, so a number dictated in words — "plus four four, seven seven oh oh, nine one one, nine one one" — is the number it spells'. That claim is true only for the international spelling; the national one, which is how people actually write a domestic number, is not covered, and the comment reads as though the class is closed.

Fix: give the phone validator a national-format path rather than relying on '+' surviving the candidate. Either (1) parse each candidate a second time under a configured default region (a `--phone-region`/yml setting, defaulting to the source cluster's lc_* or to a documented value) so '07911 123456' and its spelled form parse, or (2) have candidates.go emit an additional '+<cc>' candidate for a national-format digit run under that same region hint. (1) is the smaller change and keeps candidates.go honest about only respelling, not guessing a country. Whichever is chosen, add a regression under testdata/regressions/ with a national-format number both plain and dictated, and correct the ValidPhone doc comment so it states the region limit instead of implying the dictated case is closed. Note this is a recall change against ADR-010/T1, so it needs the T1 review internal/classify/CLAUDE.md demands.

still_leaking.attack: R2-04 / A9b replay — an SSN stored as `bigint` (`taxref`) and a phone stored as `numeric` (`msisdn`), no Luhn-valid card in the table so the second net's other numeric entry cannot fire. 300 rows, table `payroll`.
still_leaking.reproduction:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0
./run.sh a9b a9b_numeric.sql
./check.sh a9b '78051' '44770090'
docker exec rt0-tgt psql -U ls -d tgt_a9b -c 'select id,taxref,msisdn from payroll order by id limit 4'
# diagnostic run that isolates the cause (same attack, values spread instead of sequential,
# no personal neighbour at all):  ./run.sh diag diag_nodense_nocorrob.sql
#   payroll3(taxref bigint = 100000000 + floor(random()*799999999), amount numeric), 300 rows
still_leaking.fix:
STILL LEAKS. Exit 0. `msisdn` is saved by its name matching phone and is masked to a fake number, but `taxref` reports 'no name or value signal' and all 300 SSNs cross verbatim (300 hits for '78051'; target reads `1 | 78051001`). The diagnostic run leaks identically (exit 0, 300 sequential-free random 9-digit SSNs in the target).

Root cause on this tree is no longer 'no validator' — internal/verify/validators.go:344-349 now has the digits entry (textsig.ValidNationalIDDigits, minRatio=nationalIDDigitsThreshold 0.97, sequenceExempt, requiresCorroboration). Two of its three gates are what let the value through, and the two runs separate them:
  1. sequenceExempt / digitRange. The replay's values are 78051001..78051300, a dense block, so the column is exempted before its ratio is scored. That exemption is defensible for a surrogate key, but a block of sequentially ISSUED identifiers (a payroll import, a benefits batch, a migrated legacy range) is exactly as dense and exactly as personal, and it is exempt by construction.
  2. requiresCorroboration. The diagnostic run's values are sparse, so density does not save them — the column leaks anyway because nothing in `payroll3` corroborates: rules.yml's national_id name pattern does not match `taxref`, and `amount` is not a proven personal column. Comparing this with the A9b variant below (same sparse values PLUS a proven email neighbour → exit 9, refused), corroboration is the load-bearing gate, and it makes the control conditional on the attacker being careless enough to leave a recognisable personal column in the same table.

Fix, in two parts and both are ADR-level recall trades, not patches:
  a. Narrow sequenceExempt so it exempts a dense run only when the column is also the table's key or is provably generated (a `serial`/identity default, or an `int`/`bigint` column with a sequence attached) — internal/verify already reads enough catalog to know. A dense non-key bigint column with no sequence behind it is a loaded block, not a counter, and should be scored rather than skipped.
  b. requiresCorroboration should accept a third corroborator that does not depend on a neighbour: the column's own value distribution passing the SSA exclusion ranges at ratio 1.0 while being neither a date nor a generated sequence, over a sample large enough to matter. Failing that, the honest alternative is to stop calling this a control for the uncorroborated case and say so in THREAT_MODEL.md T1 — the tree today reports 'no name or value signal' for a column of real SSNs, which reads as a finding of absence.
File under T-0195's neighbourhood; it needs the T1 review and a TestPagilaPrecisionAndRecall measurement, not a quiet threshold edit.

still_leaking.attack: R2-05 / A10 replay — a person's full name the dictionary does not carry, in a column called `label` whose name matches no rule, in a table with no other personal column: Khmer, Lao and Amharic transliterations (Sokhem Chanthavy, Bounmy Phimmasone, Tesfaye Gebreselassie, Rithy Sopheak, Khamla Vongsa). 300 rows, table `entries`.
still_leaking.fix:
STILL LEAKS, and nothing about it has changed since round 2. Exit 0, 60 hits for each of the five names, column reported 'no name or value signal'.

This remains the acknowledged THREAT_MODEL.md T1 residual (line 41: 'a name in a language the dictionary does not carry, in a column named in that language, with no other signal in the table'), so I report it as reproducing rather than as new. What has NOT happened is either of the two cheap things round 2 asked for:
  1. The reason string is still the bare 'no name or value signal'. For a character column that was sampled and matched nothing, that is a finding of absence printed where only absence of evidence exists, and it is the same sentence the tool prints for an integer column it never looked inside. Change it for the sampled-character case to something that says what actually happened — 'nothing recognised in 200 samples; not proof the column is impersonal'. This is a render/reasons change (internal/classify/reasons.go), costs no recall, and is the honest half.
  2. unknownColumnsBesideCertain still fires only inside a table that already holds a `certain` person-identifying column, which is precisely the table this attack does not have. A table whose only unexplained column is a short, low-cardinality, non-unique character column with no type conflict is worth a `possible`, or at minimum a printed prompt in interactive mode. That is a recall/precision trade — it belongs in the tracker as an ADR question under the T1 residual, not in this fix round.

still_leaking.attack: NEW VARIANT of R2-01/A2 — the surviving `contact` hole taken off the reserved drama range and made ordinary: REAL, valid national-format UK phone numbers, both dictated in words (`contact`) and written plainly with spaces and brackets (`kontaktnr`, an abbreviation in another language, which is the column-name half of the surface). No obfuscation of any kind in `kontaktnr`. 300 rows, table `tickets`.
still_leaking.reproduction:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0
cat a2v_phone.sql   # tickets(id, contact text, kontaktnr text, note text)
                    # contact:   'oh seven nine one one one two three four five six' | 'oh two oh seven nine four six oh nine five eight'
                    # kontaktnr: '07911 123456' | '020 7946 0958' | '(0161) 496 0123'
./run.sh a2v a2v_phone.sql
./check.sh a2v 'oh seven nine one one' 'oh two oh seven nine four six' '07911 123456' '020 7946 0958' '0161'
docker exec rt0-tgt psql -U ls -d tgt_a2v -c 'select id,contact,kontaktnr from tickets order by id limit 3'
still_leaking.fix:
LEAKED, and this is the severe form of the A2 residual. Exit 0. Both columns report 'no name or value signal'. 150 hits each for the two dictated numbers, 100 hits each for '07911 123456', '020 7946 0958' and '0161' — the target rows read `1 | oh two oh seven nine four six oh nine five eight | 020 7946 0958`. A plain, correctly formatted domestic phone number in a column called `kontaktnr` is copied to the target verbatim under a green tick, with no obfuscation and no exotic encoding. (The only column masked in the table was `note`, on its name.)

Same root cause as the A2 residual — PhoneRegionHint = "ZZ" in internal/textsig/textsig.go:49 means libphonenumber parses nothing that is not already +E.164, so every national spelling scores zero, and Dict.Prose cannot see a string of digits or digit-words. The variant matters because it removes the defence that the A2 case was contrived: the attacker did not have to spell anything out, and `kontaktnr`/`contact` are names a real ticketing or CRM schema would use.

Fix as in the A2 entry: parse candidates a second time under a configured default region (flag + yml, surfaced in the reasons output so the operator can see which region was assumed), so both '07911 123456' and its dictated form are a phone; keep the strong/any-hit-fails footing the text phone entry already has in internal/verify/validators.go. Pin both spellings in testdata/regressions/, and pin a national-format number under a DIFFERENT region as a non-hit so the region assumption is visible rather than silent. ValidPhone's doc comment ('a national-format column reaches the classifier through its name, at possible, and is masked anyway') is the assumption this variant falsifies — a name that is not in rules.yml gets nothing — so that comment and THREAT_MODEL.md T1 need correcting alongside the code.

still_leaking.attack: NEW VARIANT of R2-05/A10 — the same dictionary-miss class taken one step further: the names written in their NATIVE SCRIPT (Amharic, Khmer, Lao, Thai) in a column whose NAME is also in that script (`ስም`, Amharic for 'name'), in a table with no other personal column. 300 rows, table `registrations`.
still_leaking.reproduction:

cat a10v_script.sql  # registrations(id serial pk, "ስም" text, qty int)
                     # values: 'ተስፋዬ ገብረሥላሴ','ብርሃኑ አበበ','សុខេម ចន្ថាវី','ຄຳລາ ວົງສາ','ริทธี โสภาค'
./run.sh a10v a10v_script.sql
./check.sh a10v 'ተስፋዬ' 'ብርሃኑ' 'សុខេម' 'ຄຳລາ' 'ริทธี'
docker exec rt0-tgt psql -U ls -d tgt_a10v -c 'select id,"ስም" from registrations order by id limit 3'
still_leaking.fix:
LEAKED. Exit 0, 60 hits for each of the five names, and the column is reported as 'public.registrations.ስም: no name or value signal'. The tool handled the non-ASCII identifier and the UTF-8 values correctly throughout — it quoted and recreated the column, sampled it, and then said it found nothing — so this is a recall miss, not a mishandling.

It is the same T1 residual as A10, with one addition that is a concrete, bounded fix rather than an unbounded dictionary problem: rules.yml's name patterns are ASCII-only, so a column literally named 'name' in Amharic, Khmer, Lao, Thai, Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic or CJK matches nothing. Widening the NAME rule pack to carry the word for name/surname/address/phone/email in the twenty or so scripts a production schema plausibly uses is finite, testable, and costs no value-side recall — unlike widening names.txt, which the round-2 note rightly refused. That alone would have caught this table.

Two things to do, both filed rather than slipped in: (1) add non-ASCII name-rule entries to rules.yml with a regression fixture per script, and state in internal/classify/CLAUDE.md that the rule pack is expected to be multilingual so the next reviewer sees the gap; (2) the reason-string change from the A10 entry applies here with extra force — a column named in a script the rule pack cannot read should not report the same sentence as a column the rules examined and cleared.

still_leaking.attack: One new variant of R2-06, since the fix it landed rests entirely on pg_postmaster_start_time() being readable by the source role: deny the source role that function too (a hardened production cluster that revokes monitoring functions from PUBLIC — the same class of hardening the original finding's premise assumes for pg_control_system), then reach the same cluster over the socket again. With both identity functions denied, Source.ClusterID returns "" with a nil error (internal/pg/source.go:236-240 swallows any non-context error), the gate's clusterKnown is false and sourceSystemID is "", so Target.Gate falls through to the last arm — targetRef.SameCluster(source), a comparison of normalised host:port — and 'unix:/private/.../sock' does not equal 'localhost'. Rule 1's fail-closed sameCatalog arm cannot save it either, because it only fires when currentDB == source.Database and the target database is called newprod, not app.
still_leaking.reproduction:
# same lab as above, still running
psql postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/app -c "REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_postmaster_start_time() FROM public;"
psql -tA postgres://reader:pw@127.0.0.1:15600/app -c 'select pg_postmaster_start_time()'   # -> permission denied
psql postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/postgres -c 'DROP DATABASE newprod' -c 'CREATE DATABASE newprod'
psql postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod -f $B/schema.sql        # empty production database
export LAZYSLICE_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
$B/lazyslice --source 'postgres://reader:pw@127.0.0.1:15600/app' \
  --target "postgres://postgres@/newprod?host=$B/sock&port=15600" --yes --no-config -n 5
#  source app on 127.0.0.1 as reader (flag) - --source
#  target newprod on /private/.../sock - --target
#  (NO same-cluster line: grep -c 'same cluster' = 0)
#  dropping public.orders in the target
#  dropping public.customers in the target
#  public.customers: 5 rows / public.orders: 20 rows
#  exit=0
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod -c 'select count(*) from customers'   # -> 5
still_leaking.fix:
Three changes, in order of how much they buy.
(1) internal/pg/source.go: make the cluster identity degrade field by field instead of all-or-nothing. sqlClusterID is one SELECT, so a permission error on pg_postmaster_start_time() kills the whole row and the identity becomes "" — the state the gate reads as 'unknown' and then resolves by endpoint spelling, which is exactly what an alias changes. Wrap each field so an unreadable one is the empty string rather than an error, e.g. compute the start time in a scalar subquery guarded by has_function_privilege('pg_postmaster_start_time()','EXECUTE') (and the same for pg_control_system), so a role that lost one function still contributes the fields it can read. On this cluster the target side could read everything; only the source side collapsed.
(2) internal/pg/target.go, Target.Gate: the last arm of the SameCluster switch (line 263, targetRef.SameCluster(source)) must not be allowed to answer 'different cluster' from an endpoint spelling when both catalog identities are unknown. When clusterUnknown() is true, SameCluster should be reported as unknown-and-treated-as-true for the purposes of the warning and of T-0184's headless refusal — i.e. warn 'the target may be on the source's own cluster: neither server would identify itself' — rather than silently false. A false negative here is a production write; a false positive is one extra warning line. The same reasoning already justifies the sameCatalog fail-closed arm, but that arm is gated on currentDB == source.Database and so covers only the case where the two databases share a name; the mid-migration case this attempt used (app -> newprod on one cluster) is outside it.
(3) Close the precondition: add `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_control_system() TO lazyslice_ro;` to the recommended-role snippet in ARCHITECTURE.md §9 and in internal/core/run.go's CodeRoleWritable message (round-2 fix item 3, not yet landed). With system_identifier readable on the source side, neither this variant nor the original R2-06 has anything to work with.
Regression test: internal/pg/gate_integration_test.go should assert that a source whose role can execute neither pg_control_system nor pg_postmaster_start_time still yields SameCluster == true for a target on that same cluster reached over a different transport.

still_leaking.attack: Round2 item 0 (A2) — six columns with no name-rule crafted to miss every regex/parser: full name in `label`; obfuscated email in `handle2`; phone-in-words in `contact`; interleaved-spelling UK NI number in `ident`; dotted payment card in `pan`; wordy address in `whereabouts`. Round2 found only `ident` still leaked (60/60 hits verbatim).
still_leaking.reproduction: cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-3/natid-test; CREATE TABLE records(id int PK, label text, handle2 text, contact text, ident text, pan text, whereabouts text); insert 3 rows matching round2's shapes; run /tmp/lazyslice-review --root public.records --take 10 --yes --no-config; SELECT * FROM records on target
still_leaking.fix: PARTIALLY FIXED, ONE NEW LEAK FOUND. `ident` (the round2 finding) is now fixed: classify reports "2/3 samples parse as national identifiers ... masked as free_text" and the target holds fabricated garble text, not the source values — T-0187's row-path wiring works. label/handle2/pan/whereabouts also masked correctly. But `contact` (the phone spelled entirely in words, e.g. 'oh seven seven oh oh one two three four') crosses completely verbatim, exit 0, classify says "no name or value signal". Root cause, isolated to a single-column table to rule out interference (contact-only table, same result): internal/classify's free_text rule is `{pipeline.CatFreeText, phraseProse, false, func(d *textsig.Dict, s string) bool { return d.Prose(s) }}` and `Dict.Prose` (internal/textsig/dict.go:195) requires `d.ContainsName(s)` on top of the >=6-word floor — so prose with zero digits and zero dictionary-name words (a phone spelled entirely as number-words) fails Prose and there is no phone-in-words validator at all, so the column falls to `none` and copies verbatim. Fix: either give Prose (or a new rule) a shape check for "mostly number-words" (a small word-to-digit dictionary: zero..nine, oh, double, etc.), or loosen the free_text gate so a long run of purely lowercase words with no punctuation and no stopword-sentence shape also qualifies, corroborated by the neighbouring-column rule the way label/whereabouts already are. Not filed as a tracker task per this task's 'do not change any repo file' instruction; reporting only.

Nothing leaks into lazyslice.yml, the transcript, --json or the temp files: this is a target-rows-only leak.

Root cause, verified, and it is NOT the one round 2 predicted. The two-part fix round 2 asked for did land: internal/verify/validators.go:346-349 now has a `digits: true` national_id entry, and textsig.ValidNationalIDDigits('78051001') returns true (probed against internal/textsig). Two guards on that one entry both hold it back:
  1. `sequenceExempt: true` plus digitRange.dense() (internal/verify/secondnet.go:349, :259-277). taxref's values are 78051001..78051300 — 300 values in a span of 300 — so the column reads as a generated sequence and the entry is skipped before its ratio is ever scored. Any real payroll whose national-ID block is issued contiguously has exactly this shape.
  2. `requiresCorroboration: true` (secondnet.go:357, corroborated() at :298-301) needs `NameMatchedNationalID` or `TableHasLikelyPersonalColumn`. `msisdn` matched phone BY NAME ONLY with no value samples, and internal/classify/classify.go:848-849 gives a name-only, sample-less match `ConfPossible` — masked, but strictly below the `ConfLikely` floor internal/classify/classify.go:1178 counts for TableHasLikelyPersonalColumn. Count `w.d.Masked` (or `Confidence >= ConfPossible` restricted to identifiesAPerson categories) in the neighbour tally at classify.go:1178, not `>= ConfLikely`; the ConfLikely floor belongs to the neighbouring-column raising rule, not to this signal, and reusing one number for both is what made a masked phone column invisible. (b) The dense-range exemption must not apply once corroboration is present: at secondnet.go:349, skip on `dense` only when `!corroborated`. A dense block of nine-digit values in a table that already holds a masked personal column is the leak this entry exists for, and the 'it is a generated sequence' reading is the weaker of the two. (c) Add the missing recall side on the classify path too — internal/classify/classify.go:355-370's own comment concedes the `text`/`digits` split is owed (tracker T-0195) and that 'an SSN stored as bigint with no name hit is still none here'; T-0195 is the right home, but the comment should stop pointing at internal/verify's digits entry as the compensating control until (a) and (b) land, because today it is not one.

still_leaking.fix:
PARTLY FIXED, STILL LEAKED. The validator set behind strongCatalogHit / strongHit was genuinely widened (commit 986091d, T-0189): internal/plan/ddlliteral.go strongValidators and internal/verify/catalog.go strongCatalogHit now run ten validators including NameShape, addressLiteralShape and ProseName. The name CHECK is exit 13 ('parses as person_name'), the address CHECK is exit 13 ('parses as address'). But c_notes exits 0 and the target catalog holds:
  ck_notes_free|CHECK (((notes IS NULL) OR (notes <> 'Priya Raghunathan disclosed her HIV diagnosis on 2019-04-02'::text)))

Root cause, verified. The widened list still has no entry for CatSpecial, and the free_text entry it does have is Dict.ProseName (internal/textsig/dict.go:219), which requires >= 6 whitespace fields AND an adjacent given-name/surname pair from names.txt. The literal has 8 fields, and `priya` IS in names.txt (line 9418) as a given name, but `raghunathan` is in neither list, so the adjacency never fires and ProseName returns false. Dict.NameShape on the whole 8-word string is false for the same reason. The literal therefore matches nothing and is replayed verbatim onto a column lazyslice itself masked as free_text.

Fix. (a) The DDL literal boundary must cover every category the row boundary masks: special_category has no validator at all in either strongHit or strongCatalogHit, which is the gap THREAT_MODEL.md T1's amendment claims is closed. Add the special-category term list the row path uses (the rules.yml special_category vocabulary — diagnosis/HIV/religion/union/orientation terms) as a literal validator in both functions. (b) ProseName is the wrong shape test for a DDL literal. Its dictionary-adjacency narrowing exists to stop a COLUMN OF prose being scored at exit 9 across thousands of rows; a single string literal written into a CHECK on a column the run classified personal is not a false-positive risk of the same size. For literals, fall back to plain Dict.Prose (>= 6 words with a dictionary hit) and, where that is still too noisy, fail towards the operator rather than towards silence — print the object and require an explicit --allow-ddl-literal opt-out, the way --allow-type-literal already works for enums and domains (commit a29b625). (c) The general rule, worth writing into THREAT_MODEL.md T1 in these words: the list of categories the DDL boundary recognises must be kept EQUAL to the list the row boundary masks, and a column the run decided to mask should make any literal in its own constraints refusable by default, not only literals that re-parse as a recognised shape.

HALF FIXED; THE MODULE HALF STILL LEAKS. Output: `ERROR-RETURN: err=cannot mask "victim.canary@bigcorp.example": unsupported shape` — mask.Apply returns the masker's error verbatim.

What landed: part (a) of round 2's fix is in. internal/transform/codes.go Refusal.Error() no longer interpolates r.Reason; it calls reasonSummary(r.Reason), which returns maskReason(err) for the module's own sentinel errors and otherwise 'an error of type %T (its message is withheld because it may quote the value)'. So the CLI half is closed and no lazyslice run prints this.

What did not: mask/mask.go Apply -> maskCell still does `out, err = m.Mask(h, in, c); if err != nil { return Value{}, err }`, passing the third-party error straight out of the public module. mask/ is importable on its own (it has its own go.mod, and ADR-006 is the reason), so its contract cannot depend on the parent binary's redaction — the same argument that justified adding the recover two lines above applies unchanged to the error return beside it. Fix: in maskCell, wrap the masker's error the way the panic is wrapped — a new ErrMaskerRefused naming the masker id and the category and the error's %T, with the original kept only behind an explicitly opt-in unwrap (or not kept at all). Part (b) of round 2's fix is also still owed: cmd/lazyslice/main.go renderSafe is still an allowlist of two error types to scrub with `return err.Error()` as its default, so every new error type in the tree is value-bearing until someone notices; invert it as round 2 described.
